# PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS] Contents of this Part

## I WITNESSES AND DEPOSITIONS

## Scope of this Section

## 34.1

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.1] (1) This Section of this Part provides –

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.1] (a) for the circumstances in which a person may be required to attend court to give evidence or to produce a document; and

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.1] (b) for a party to obtain evidence before a hearing to be used at the hearing. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.1] (2) In this Section, reference to a hearing includes a reference to the trial. ## Witness summonses

## 34.2

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.2] (1) A witness summons is a document issued by the court requiring a witness to –

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.2] (a) attend court to give evidence; or

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.2] (b) produce documents to the court. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.2] (2) A witness summons must be in the relevant practice form. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.2] (3) There must be a separate witness summons for each witness. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.2] (4) A witness summons may require a witness to produce documents to the court either –

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.2] (a) on the date fixed for a hearing; or

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.2] (b) on such date as the court may direct. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.2] (5) The only documents that a summons under this rule can require a person to produce before a hearing are documents which that person could be required to produce at the hearing. ## Issue of a witness summons

## 34.3

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.3] (1) A witness summons is issued on the date entered on the summons by the court. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.3] (2) A party must obtain permission from the court where he wishes to –

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.3] (a) have a summons issued less than 7 days before the date of the trial;

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.3] (b) have a summons issued for a witness to attend court to give evidence or to produce documents on any date except the date fixed for the trial; or

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.3] (c) have a summons issued for a witness to attend court to give evidence or to produce documents at any hearing except the trial. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.3] (3) A witness summons must be issued by –

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.3] (a) the court where the case is proceeding; or

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.3] (b) the court where the hearing in question will be held. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.3] (4) The court may set aside (GL) or vary a witness summons issued under this rule. ## Witness summons in aid of inferior court or of tribunal

## 34.4

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.4] (1) The court may issue a witness summons in aid of an inferior court or of a tribunal. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.4] (2) The court which issued the witness summons under this rule may set it aside. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.4] (3) In this rule, ‘inferior court or tribunal’ means any court or tribunal that does not have power to issue a witness summons in relation to proceedings before it. ## Time for serving a witness summons

## 34.5

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.5] (1) The general rule is that a witness summons is binding if it is served at least 7 days before the date on which the witness is required to attend before the court or tribunal. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.5] (2) The court may direct that a witness summons shall be binding although it will be served less than 7 days before the date on which the witness is required to attend before the court or tribunal. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.5] (3) A witness summons which is –

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.5] (a) served in accordance with this rule; and

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.5] (b) requires the witness to attend court to give evidence,

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.5] is binding until the conclusion of the hearing at which the attendance of the witness is required. ## Who is to serve a witness summons

## 34.6

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.6] (1) A witness summons is to be served by the court unless the party on whose behalf it is issued indicates in writing, when he asks the court to issue the summons, that he wishes to serve it himself. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.6] (2) Where the court is to serve the witness summons, the party on whose behalf it is issued must deposit, in the court office, the money to be paid or offered to the witness under rule 34.7. ## Right of witness to travelling expenses and compensation for loss of time

## 34.7

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.7] At the time of service of a witness summons the witness must be offered or paid –

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.7] (a) a sum reasonably sufficient to cover his expenses in travelling to and from the court; and

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.7] (b) such sum by way of compensation for loss of time as may be specified in Practice Direction 34A. ## Fines imposed under section 55 of the County Courts Act 1984

## 34.7A

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.7A] If a person has failed to comply with an order under section 55 of the County Courts Act 1984 but can demonstrate any reason why they should not be (or should not have been) fined for failure to comply with the order, the court may direct that that person give evidence by witness statement, affidavit or otherwise. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.7A] (Part 70 contains general rules about fines imposed under the County Courts Act 1984.)

## Evidence by deposition

## 34.8

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.8] (1) A party may apply for an order for a person to be examined before the hearing takes place. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.8] (2) A person from whom evidence is to be obtained following an order under this rule is referred to as a ‘deponent’ and the evidence is referred to as a ‘deposition’. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.8] (3) An order under this rule shall be for a deponent to be examined on oath before –

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.8] (a) a judge;

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.8] (b) an examiner of the court; or

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.8] (c) such other person as the court appoints. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.8] (Rule 34.15 makes provision for the appointment of examiners of the court)

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.8] (4) The order may require the production of any document which the court considers is necessary for the purposes of the examination. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.8] (5) The order must state the date, time and place of the examination. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.8] (6) At the time of service of the order the deponent must be offered or paid –

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.8] (a) a sum reasonably sufficient to cover his expenses in travelling to and from the place of examination; and

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.8] (b) such sum by way of compensation for loss of time as may be specified in Practice Direction 34A. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.8] (7) Where the court makes an order for a deposition to be taken, it may also order the party who obtained the order to serve a witness statement or witness summary in relation to the evidence to be given by the person to be examined. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.8] (Part 32 contains the general rules about witness statements and witness summaries)

## Conduct of examination

## 34.9

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.9] (1) Subject to any directions contained in the order for examination, the examination must be conducted in the same way as if the witness were giving evidence at a trial. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.9] (2) If all the parties are present, the examiner may conduct the examination of a person not named in the order for examination if all the parties and the person to be examined consent. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.9] (3) The examiner may conduct the examination in private if he considers it appropriate to do so. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.9] (4) The examiner must ensure that the evidence given by the witness is recorded in full. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.9] (5) The examiner must send a copy of the deposition –

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.9] (a) to the person who obtained the order for the examination of the witness; and

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.9] (b) to the court where the case is proceeding. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.9] (6) The party who obtained the order must send each of the other parties a copy of the deposition which he receives from the examiner. ## Enforcing attendance of witness

## 34.10

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.10] (1) If a person served with an order to attend before an examiner –

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.10] (a) fails to attend; or

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.10] (b) refuses to be sworn for the purpose of the examination or to answer any lawful question or produce any document at the examination,

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.10] a certificate of his failure or refusal, signed by the examiner, must be filed by the party requiring the deposition. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.10] (2) On the certificate being filed, the party requiring the deposition may apply to the court for an order requiring that person to attend or to be sworn or to answer any question or produce any document, as the case may be. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.10] (3) An application for an order under this rule may be made without notice. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.10] (4) The court may order the person against whom an order is made under this rule to pay any costs resulting from his failure or refusal. ## Use of deposition at a hearing

## 34.11

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.11] (1) A deposition ordered under rule 34.8 may be given in evidence at a hearing unless the court orders otherwise. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.11] (2) A party intending to put in evidence a deposition at a hearing must serve notice of his intention to do so on every other party. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.11] (3) He must serve the notice at least 21 days before the day fixed for the hearing. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.11] (4) The court may require a deponent to attend the hearing and give evidence orally. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.11] (5) Where a deposition is given in evidence at trial, it shall be treated as if it were a witness statement for the purposes of rule 32.13 (availability of witness statements for inspection). ## Restrictions on subsequent use of deposition taken for the purpose of any hearing except the trial

## 34.12

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.12] (1) Where the court orders a party to be examined about his or any other assets for the purpose of any hearing except the trial, the deposition may be used only for the purpose of the proceedings in which the order was made. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.12] (2) However, it may be used for some other purpose –

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.12] (a) by the party who was examined;

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.12] (b) if the party who was examined agrees; or

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.12] (c) if the court gives permission. ## Where a person to be examined is out of the jurisdiction – letter of request

## 34.13

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.13] (1) This rule applies where a party wishes to take a deposition from a person who is –

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.13] (a) out of the jurisdiction;

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.13] (1A) The High Court may order the issue of a letter of request to the judicial authorities of the country in which the proposed deponent is. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.13] (2) A letter of request is a request to a judicial authority to take the evidence of that person, or arrange for it to be taken. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.13] (3) The High Court may make an order under this rule in relation to county court proceedings and tribunal proceedings. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.13] (4) If the government of a country allows a person appointed by the High Court to examine a person in that country, the High Court may make an order appointing a special examiner for that purpose. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.13] (5) A person may be examined under this rule on oath or affirmation or in accordance with any procedure permitted in the country in which the examination is to take place. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.13] (6) If the High Court makes an order for the issue of a letter of request, the party who sought the order must file with the Foreign Process Section of the Central Office of the High Court in the Royal Courts of Justice –

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.13] (a) the following documents and, except where paragraph (7) applies, a translation of them –

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.13] (i) a draft letter of request;

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.13] (ii) a statement of the issues relevant to the proceedings;

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.13] (iii) a list of questions or the subject matter of questions to be put to the person to be examined; and

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.13] (b) an undertaking to be responsible for the Secretary of State’s expenses. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.13] (7) There is no need to file a translation if –

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.13] (a) English is one of the official languages of the country where the examination is to take place; or

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.13] (b) a practice direction has specified that country as a country where no translation is necessary. ## Letter of request – Proceeds of Crime Act 2002

## 34.13A

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.13A] (1) This rule applies where a party to existing or contemplated proceedings in –

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.13A] (a) the High Court; or

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.13A] (b) a magistrates’ court,

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.13A] under Part 5 of the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 3 (civil recovery of the proceeds etc. of unlawful conduct) wishes to take a deposition from a person who is out of the jurisdiction. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.13A] (2) The High Court may, on the application of such a party, order the issue of a letter of request to the judicial authorities of the country in which the proposed deponent is. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.13A] (3) Paragraphs (4) to (7) of rule 34.13 shall apply irrespective of where the proposed deponent is. ## Fees and expenses of examiner of the court

## 34.14

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.14] (1) An examiner of the court may charge a fee for the examination. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.14] (2) He need not send the deposition to the court unless the fee is paid. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.14] (3) The examiner’s fees and expenses must be paid by the party who obtained the order for examination. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.14] (4) If the fees and expenses due to an examiner are not paid within a reasonable time, he may report that fact to the court. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.14] (5) The court may order the party who obtained the order for examination to deposit in the court office a specified sum in respect of the examiner’s fees and, where it does so, the examiner will not be asked to act until the sum has been deposited. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.14] (6) An order under this rule does not affect any decision as to the party who is ultimately to bear the costs of the examination. ## Examiners of the court

## 34.15

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.15] (1) The Lord Chancellor shall appoint persons to be examiners of the court. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.15] (2) The persons appointed shall be barristers or solicitor-advocates who have been practising for a period of not less than three years. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.15] (3) The Lord Chancellor may revoke an appointment at any time. ## II EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS

## Scope and interpretation

## 34.16

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.16] (1) This Section applies to an application for an order under the 1975 Act for evidence to be obtained. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.16] (2) In this Section 5 –

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.16] (a) ‘the 1975 Act’ means the Evidence (Proceedings in Other Jurisdictions) Act 1975( 2 );

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.16] the Hague Evidence Convention” means the Hague Convention of 18 March 1970 on the Taking of Evidence Abroad in Civil or Commercial Matters

## Application for order

## 34.17

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.17] (1) An application for an order under the 1975 Act for evidence to be obtained must be made to the High Court and may be made without notice. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.17] (2) The application may be made either—

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.17] (a )by an application notice under Part 23, which must be—

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.17] (i) supported by written evidence; and

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.17] (ii)accompanied by the request as a result of which the application is made, and where appropriate, a translation of the request into English; or

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.17] (b) where—

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.17] (i) the requesting state is a party to the Hague Evidence Convention, by a Letter of Request using the Model Form published by the Permanent Bureau of the Hague Conference on Private International Law (which is annexed to Practice Direction 34A); or

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.17] (ii) the requesting state is not a party to the Hague Evidence Convention, by a Letter of Request submitted via the Foreign and Commonwealth Office. ## Examination

## 34.18

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.18] (1) The court may order an examination to be taken before –

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.18] (a) any fit and proper person nominated by the person applying for the order;

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.18] (b) an examiner of the court; or

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.18] (c) any other person whom the court considers suitable. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.18] (2) Unless the court orders otherwise –

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.18] (a) the examination will be taken as provided by rule 34.9; and

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.18] (b) rule 34.10 applies. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.18] (3) The court may make an order under rule 34.14 for payment of the fees and expenses of the examination. ## Dealing with deposition

## 34.19

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.19] (1) The examiner must send the deposition of the witness to the Senior Master unless the court orders otherwise. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.19] (2) The Senior Master will –

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.19] (a) give a certificate sealed with the seal of the Senior Courts for use out of the jurisdiction identifying the following documents –

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.19] (i) the request;

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.19] (ii) the order of the court for examination; and

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.19] (iii) the deposition of the witness; and

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.19] (b) send the certificate and the documents referred to in paragraph (a) to –

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.19] (i) the Secretary of State; or

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.19] (ii) where the request was sent to the Senior Master by another person in accordance with a Civil Procedure Convention, to that other person,

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.19] for transmission to the court or tribunal requesting the examination. ## Claim to privilege

## 34.20

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.20] (1) This rule applies where –

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.20] (a) a witness claims to be exempt from giving evidence on the ground specified in section 3(1)(b) of the 1975 Act; and

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.20] (b) That claim is not supported or conceded as referred to in section 3(2) of that Act. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.20] (2) The examiner may require the witness to give the evidence which he claims to be exempt from giving. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.20] (3) Where the examiner does not require the witness to give that evidence, the court may order the witness to do so. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.20] (4) An application for an order under paragraph (3) may be made by the person who obtained the order under section 2 of the 1975 Act. [PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.20] (5) Where such evidence is taken –

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.20] (a) it must be contained in a document separate from the remainder of the deposition;

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.20] (b) the examiner will send to the Senior Master –

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.20] (i) the deposition; and

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.20] (ii) a signed statement setting out the claim to be exempt and the ground on which it was made;

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.20] (6) On receipt of the statement referred to in paragraph (5)(b)(ii), the Senior Master will –

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.20] (a) retain the document containing the part of the witness’s evidence to which the claim to be exempt relates; and

[PART 34 – WITNESSES, DEPOSITIONS AND EVIDENCE FOR FOREIGN COURTS > 34.20] (b) send the statement and a request to determine that claim to the foreign court or tribunal together with the documents referred to in rule 34.17.
